name: Vancomycin
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Intravenous vancomycin needs kidney-based dose adjustment guided by serum concentrations. The US label sets an initial dose of no less than 15 mg/kg at any level of kidney function, then dosing by measured levels; the 2020 consensus guideline favors area-under-the-curve (AUC) guided monitoring.
kidney_function_basis: Label gives no fixed eGFR or CrCl bands; dosing is concentration-guided.

bands.recommendation: Adults: usual 2 g/day (0.5 g every 6 hours or 1 g every 12 hours) for normal function, then adjust to serum concentrations (label).
Initial dose no less than 15 mg/kg; then extend interval and adjust by serum concentrations (label).
Initial dose no less than 15 mg/kg; maintenance by serum concentrations (label).
Functionally anephric: 15 mg/kg initial dose; measure level at 24 hours to guide further dosing (label).

hd: Label: 'poorly removed by dialysis' and anephric dosing as above. The 2020 consensus guideline addresses dosing with intermittent hemodialysis and recommends level-guided maintenance; reviewer to transcribe its specific dosing (see notes).
pd: Vancomycin enters peritoneal dialysis fluid (label). No PD dose in the label. Specialist input; dose by levels.
crrt: No data in label. Consensus guideline covers continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) dosing with level monitoring; specialist input.
dialyzable: Label: poorly removed by dialysis. Note: high-flux membranes remove more; see notes.
monitoring: Serum concentrations (AUC-guided per consensus; trough per label), serum creatinine; nephrotoxicity risk rises with other nephrotoxins.

pediatric.approved_ages: Indicated in pediatric patients (label). This premixed product is not recommended when the needed dose is not 500 mg, 750 mg, 1 g, 1.25 g or 1.5 g; use another formulation.
pediatric.usual_dose: Age 1 month and older, normal kidney function: 10 mg/kg per dose every 6 hours (label).
pediatric.max_dose: Label gives no separate pediatric cap; do not exceed the adult daily dose without level guidance.

renal.recommendation: 10 mg/kg every 6 hours; monitor levels and kidney function (label).
Initial dose no less than 15 mg/kg; maintenance by serum concentrations (label applies to 'patients with any degree of renal impairment').
Initial dose no less than 15 mg/kg; maintenance by serum concentrations.
15 mg/kg initial dose; level at 24 hours to guide dosing.

pediatric.hd: Level-guided dosing; specialist (pediatric nephrology/infectious diseases) input.
pediatric.neonates: Neonates (label): initial 15 mg/kg, then 10 mg/kg every 12 hours in the first week of life and every 8 hours thereafter up to 1 month of age.
pediatric.notes: The consensus guideline includes pediatric AUC-guided dosing; transcribe from full text after review.
pediatric.egfr_equation: Bedside Schwartz: eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m2) = 0.413 x height (cm) / serum creatinine (mg/dL)

adult: Full text of Rybak 2020 is not in PubMed Central; its specific HD, CRRT and pediatric mg/kg regimens were NOT transcribed. Please add them from the guideline tables or approve 'level-guided' wording.
Label phrase 'poorly removed by dialysis' reflects low-flux membranes; with high-flux HD substantial removal occurs (consensus guideline). Decide wording.
Selected label is the Baxter premixed injection (NDA050671); the fixed-strength limitation in the pediatric text is product-specific.
Label still recommends trough monitoring; the consensus guideline prefers AUC monitoring. Both are mentioned.
pediatric: Pediatric maximum dose not in label; consensus pediatric doses not transcribed.
